comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
A second instance, and not on `pane send`: closing a pane by hand on 2026-09-06 logged

```
intent.submitted  ClosePane { pane: "p21ep311we" }  refused: "timed out"
core.refused      "the daemon did not make that change: timed out ..."
```

and herdr had in fact closed the terminal - the bridge died a fraction of a second later
saying that terminal is not found, and the pane is gone from `muster window`. It happened
twice in three seconds, on two panes closed in a row, with 15 panes on the daemon.

That puts the fault below `pane send`: every intent goes through
`IntentSubmitter::submit` -> `HerdrClient::request`, which is the 500ms
`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`. So the contract question this card asks - what an exit code means when
the daemon did the work and the acknowledgement did not arrive in time - is the same
question for `pane.close`, and answering it only for `pane.send_input` would leave the
window itself reporting refusals for changes it made.

`a_2LMpvavhA` covers what the close's misreported failure then triggered.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster pane send` reported a timeout and the message had in fact arrived. The caller
did what a caller does with a reported failure - retried - and the receiving pane got
the same message six times.

Seen during a parallel-work round, one agent messaging another agent's pane. The
receiving agent had to work out for itself that six identical instructions were one
instruction, and said so.

## Why this is worse than a noisy log line

`a_2I7Acusq4` established that `pane send --enter` exiting 0 without submitting is a
bug, because the exit code is the only thing a script can read. This is the same
contract broken the other way: a non-zero exit on a message that landed. Both leave a
caller unable to tell what happened, and this direction is the one that causes damage
rather than silence, because the obvious response to a failed send is to send again.

It reaches further than one agent talking to another. `muster pane send` is the CLI
surface Muster offers agents for driving a window, and an agent that cannot trust the
exit code cannot safely retry anything. Instructions delivered several times are not a
cosmetic problem when the instruction is "commit" or "run the tier".

## What is not known

Whether the timeout is the send itself waiting too long for something downstream, or
whether the message is delivered and the acknowledgement is what goes missing. Nobody
has looked at where the wait actually is. Also unknown is how reproducible it is - it
appeared under a machine load average around 230, and nothing has tried it quiet.

## What a fix has to decide

What the exit code means when the pane received the bytes but nothing came back to say
so. A send that cannot confirm delivery is not the same as a send that failed, and the
caller needs those distinguished - either as separate exit codes, or by making the
acknowledgement reliable enough that a timeout really does mean nothing arrived.
title: 📮 pane send reports a timeout on a message it delivered, so a caller retries into duplicates
